title: Borrow, swap, lend: the library mindset
description: Before buying something you will use twice, ask whether it can be borrowed, swapped, hired, or shared. Ownership is only one way to have the use of a thing.

body.heading: Use is what you actually want
paragraphs: Nobody wants a drill; they want holes in the wall, twice a year. Nobody wants a carpet cleaner; they want a clean carpet, once a year. When the want is really the use, borrowing delivers everything buying does — minus the price and the storage.
Libraries lend far more than books in many places: tools, instruments, board games, even seeds. Tool libraries, hire shops, and neighbourhood groups exist for exactly the twice-a-year categories.

body.heading: Swapping keeps it social
paragraphs: Clothes swaps, book exchanges, and toy rotations turn surplus into novelty without money changing hands. A swap has a second benefit: the things you pass on go to people who will actually use them, which feels better than a bin bag.
Lending works when it is easy and clear. Lend gladly, name a return time kindly, and lend only what you could forgive losing — friendship is worth more than any ladder.

body.heading: When buying is still right
paragraphs: Things used weekly, things fitted to you, and safety equipment are usually worth owning properly. The library mindset is not anti-buying; it simply asks the ownership question first, and lets "twice a year" items be borrowed without a second thought.
Owning well-chosen things is a pleasure in itself, and borrowing is not a moral duty. The mindset simply makes ownership a decision rather than a reflex — which is where most money is saved.

takeaway: For anything you would use only occasionally, try borrow, swap, or hire before buying — you wanted the use of it, not the storage of it.
